Yoweri Museveni: President and dictator of Uganda since 1986. Museveni unified the opposition under the National Resistance Movement and started the Ugandan Bush War.

Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four.

Which of these four is the oldest release?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Edwin McMillan is a physicist. McMillan co-invented the synchrotron with Vladimir Veksler, and after the war he returned to the Berkeley Radiation Laboratory to build them.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Maud Menten is a chemist. Maud Leonora Menten (March 20, 1879 – July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
What is the atomic number of Silicon?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
In what year was Max Born?
Max Born: During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
In what year was Fermat's Last Theorem discovered?
Fermat's Last Theorem: The proposition was first stated as a theorem by Pierre de Fermat around 1637 in the margin of a copy of Arithmetica.
In what year was Selenium discovered?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
Metoprolol: Pfizer. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
Publishing: Germany. It has various divisions such as trade/retail publishing of fiction and non-fiction, educational publishing, and academic and scientific publishing.
Who is credited with discovering Malaria?
Malaria: Ronald Ross. Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Who is credited with discovering Kwashiorkor?
Kwashiorkor: Cicely Williams. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Who is credited with discovering Titanium?
Titanium: William Gregor. Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
When a message is designed to spark an immediate purchase, it's called the 'direct-response' kind of this consumer-facing practice. What is it?
Advertising is the practice and techniques employed to bring attention to a product or service.
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI unit measures electric current as one coulomb of charge passing a point per second. What unit is it?
Ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
More than 500 orb-weaving spider species, including the familiar garden spider, belong to this genus first classified in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus is a genus of common orb-weaving spiders with more than 500 species, among which are the European garden spider and the barn spider.

These shelled marine crustaceans, cousins to crabs and lobsters, spend their adult lives cemented in place filtering food from the water — and folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety. What are they?
Barnacle are arthropods of the subclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea.

Thought to be the world's most abundant bird of prey in its family, with an estimated 6.7 million individuals, this opportunistic raptor is known for its angled wings and distinctive forked tail — what is it?
Black kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.

This shield-shaped insect, native to East Asia, was accidentally introduced to Allentown, Pennsylvania in 1998 and became a major agricultural pest feeding on over 100 plant species — what insect is it?
Brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

Once thought to not really exist as a stable molecule, this compound was confirmed since around 1990 to have a real, if fleeting, existence — lasting only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature — what compound is it?
Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3.
Atomic number 17, this strongly oxidising yellow-green gas sits between fluorine and bromine on the periodic table — what element is it?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
What's the scientific family name for the group of birds that includes both doves and pigeons — stout-bodied birds with small heads and no formal distinction between the two common names?
Columbidae is a bird family consisting of doves and pigeons.
Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
First discovered in 1877 and named the following year for its unique double-beamed tail bones, this genus of long-necked sauropod dinosaur roamed Late Jurassic North America — what is it?
Diplodocus (or) is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic of North America.
This mammal family includes living species from two genera as well as extinct giants like the woolly mammoth, and was first scientifically described in 1821 — what family is it?

Elephantidae is a family of large, herbivorous proboscidean mammals which includes the living elephants (belonging to the genera Elephas and Loxodonta), as well as a number of extinct genera like Mammuthus (mammoths) and Palaeoloxodon.

The telltale earth mounds this tunneling mammal pushes to the surface come from its constantly expanding burrow system, and it feeds mainly on earthworms paralyzed by toxins in its saliva — what animal is it?
European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.
This American physician-scientist discovered genes tied to several diseases, led the Human Genome Project, and went on to direct the NIH under three presidents — who is he?
Francis Collins (born April 14, 1950) is an American physician-scientist who discovered the genes associated with a number of diseases and led the Human Genome Project.

A 1946 civilian demonstrator version of this British fighter became the world's first civilian-registered jet aircraft, decades after it debuted as the Allies' sole combat jet of World War II — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor was the first British jet fighter and the Allies' only jet aircraft to engage in combat operations during the Second World War.

This herbivorous mammal, the largest in its family of lagomorphs, nests in shallow ground depressions called 'forms' and is built for speed with long hind legs and heat-dissipating ears — what animal is it?
Hare are mammals belonging to the genus Lepus.
This American physicist threw out the wave-function collapse postulate, instead folding the observer into the same quantum state — an idea later known as the many-worlds interpretation. Who was he?
Hugh Everett III (November 11, 1930 - July 19, 1982) was an American physicist who proposed the relative state interpretation of quantum mechanics.

According to Alfred Adler, this persistent psychological feeling of being deficient compared to others — often rooted in childhood upbringing or social status — can drive a person to overcompensate. Name the concept?
Inferiority complex is a consistent feeling of inadequacy, often resulting in the belief that one is in some way deficient, or inferior, to others.
A former Chicago financial options trader, this internet entrepreneur co-founded a nonprofit free encyclopedia as well as the for-profit wiki host Fandom — who is he?
Jimmy Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.

Normally part of the healthy flora in the mouth, skin, and gut, this rod-shaped bacterium can turn destructive if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brick-colored jelly-like sputum — what's the organism?
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.

Equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometres, this astronomical distance unit is defined by how far illumination travels through a vacuum in 365.25 days — despite its name, it isn't a measure of time. What is it?
Light-year (ly or lyr), is a unit of length used to express astronomical distances and is equal to exactly 9460730472580.8 km, which is approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres or 5.88 trillion miles.
Which Australian nut-producing tree genus, an important bushfood for Aboriginal peoples, was first commercially cultivated at scale not in its native country but in Hawaii?
Macadamia is a genus of four species of trees in the flowering plant family Proteaceae.
This cone-shaped structure at the base of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from heart rate and breathing to vomiting and sneezing — what is it called?
Medulla oblongata is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.
By dividing one cell into two with an identical set of chromosomes apiece, this stage of the cell cycle keeps genetic stability intact across generations — what is it?
Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.

This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, attacking REM sleep with daytime drowsiness, sleep paralysis, and cataplexy — sudden episodes where muscle tone simply vanishes. What is it?
Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

Classified using a measurement of weight divided by the square of height, this medical condition is diagnosed when that figure exceeds 30 and is linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes — what is it?
Obesity is a medical condition, considered a disease by multiple organizations, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that it can have negative effects on health.
Pair it with aspirin and caffeine and it's a first-line remedy for mild headaches; on its own it's the active ingredient many people know as acetaminophen — what is this over-the-counter drug?
Paracetamol is an analgesic and antipyretic agent used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain.
This inflammation of the back of the throat causes a sore throat and fever, most often from a viral infection, though strep bacteria cause roughly a quarter of cases in children — name the condition?
Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx.
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

Drawing on tools from anthropology, biology, medicine, psychology, and criminology, this scientific field studies human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions, distinct from purely social commentary on the subject — what is this field called?
Sexology is the scientific study of human sexuality, including human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions.
Beginning with stem cells near the basement membrane and passing through two rounds of meiosis, this process turns germ cells into haploid sperm inside the seminiferous tubules — what is it called?
Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testicle.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.

In 1933 he won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries about the role of chromosomes in heredity, studying fruit-fly genetics after the rediscovery of Mendelian inheritance in 1900—who was this pioneering biologist?
Thomas Hunt Morgan (September 25, 1866 - December 4, 1945) was an American evolutionary biologist, geneticist, and embryologist.
Built in the Soviet Union from 1966 to 1989 for short-haul routes, this narrow-body jet earned the NATO codename 'Crusty' — which airliner is it?
Tupolev Tu-134 (NATO reporting name: Crusty) is a twin-engined, narrow-body jet airliner built in the Soviet Union for short and medium-haul routes from 1966 to 1989.

Many of these carrion-eating birds sport a bald head that stays clean while feeding and helps with temperature control — and they'll even urinate on their own legs to cool off. What kind of bird is it?
Vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion.
Atomic number 30, mined mostly from the ore sphalerite, this metal turns shiny blue-white once its surface oxidation is removed — which element?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
Nicknamed the cell's "molecular unit of currency," this energy-carrying molecule powers muscle contraction and nerve impulses, dropping to ADP or AMP when spent — what is it?
Adenosine triphosphate: Energy-carrying molecule in living cells.
Sometimes called 'emotional blindness,' this condition makes it hard to identify or describe one's own feelings, and affects roughly half of people with autism. What is it?
Alexithymia: Deficiency in understanding, processing, or describing emotions.
Nicknamed the corpse flower for its rotting-flesh stench, this Sumatran plant first bloomed in cultivation at Kew Gardens in 1889 — which species?
Amorphophallus titanum: Species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae.
NATO code-named 'Condor,' this Soviet-designed four-engine giant is the largest military transport aircraft still flying today — which aircraft?

Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Soviet military transport aircraft. Assembly of the first aircraft begun in 1979; the An-124 (which was sometimes referred to as the An-40 in the West) performed its maiden flight on 24 December 1982.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
Coined in 1814 by chemist William Hyde Wollaston, this polyatomic anion forms when carbonic acid loses a proton and plays a crucial role buffering the body's pH — what is it?
Bicarbonate: Polyatomic anion. It is a polyatomic anion with the chemical formula HCO−3.
Named in allusion to a 'Flying Fortress' that came before it, this pressurized WWII heavy bomber dropped the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Which aircraft?
Air warfare of World War II
Boeing B-29 Superfortress: US heavy bomber aircraft, 1942.
Nicknamed 'angel's trumpets' for its pendulous, fragrant blooms, this toxic nightshade-family genus is officially Extinct in the Wild yet thrives worldwide as a garden plant — which genus?
Brugmansia: Genus of flowering plants in the nightshade family.
Present in the gut or mouth of up to 60 percent of healthy adults, this opportunistic yeast turns dangerous in immunocompromised patients, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans: Species of fungus. Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
Named after a Louisiana parish and named the state's official canine in 1979, this herding breed was traditionally used to hunt feral boars — what breed is it?
Catahoula Leopard Dog: American breed of dog.
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Patented in 1967, this sympathomimetic drug helps people with asthma and other breathing disorders by acting as a bronchodilator — which substance?
Clenbuterol: Chemical compound which aids breathing.
One of the most intensively studied and intelligent cephalopods, this mollusk ranges from the Mediterranean and English coastline all the way to South Africa — which species?
Common octopus: Species of cephalopod. The common octopus (Octopus vulgaris) is a mollusk belonging to the class Cephalopoda.

Ancient Greek, Chinese, and Indian cultures lacked a concept for this, seeing art as discovery rather than invention, while the Judeo-Christian-Islamic tradition later reserved it for God alone — what mental faculty is this?
Creativity: Forming something new and somehow valuable.
Also known as jimsonweed or devil's trumpet, this poisonous nightshade plant likely native to Central America has been used both in folk medicine and, unpleasantly, as a hallucinogen — which plant?
Datura stramonium: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Nicknamed the 'businessman's trip' in the 1960s for its rapid onset and short duration, which naturally occurring tryptamine hallucinogen has long been used as a ritual entheogen?
Of the 68 species bearing this name, only the Aquilinae are genetically "true" ones — the rest just qualify as any bird of prey big enough to hunt sizeable vertebrates; what's the common name?
Eagle: Large bird of prey. Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?
A founder of modern topology who also wrote under the playful pen name "Paul Mongré," this German mathematician — Jewish and facing deportation — died by suicide with his family in 1942. Who was he?
Felix Hausdorff: German mathematician (1868–1942). Hausdorff was Jewish, and life became difficult for him and his family after the Kristallnacht of 1938.
This double-layered fold of skin covering the glans is attached by an elastic band called the frenulum and is typically fused in place at birth — what is it?
Foreskin: Retractable fold of skin which covers and protects the glans of the penis.
Nicknamed the 'stomach flu' in the US and Canada, this inflammation of the gut is most often caused in kids by rotavirus and in adults by norovirus — what is it?
Gastroenteritis: Inflammation of the stomach and small intestine.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?
Credited as the inventor of radio, this Italian engineer shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics and later set up Vatican Radio for Pope Pius XI — who is he?
Guglielmo Marconi: Italian radio-frequency engineer and inventor (1874–1937)
Despite common nicknames like 'Christmas rose' and 'Lenten rose,' this poisonous Eurasian flowering genus isn't actually related to roses at all — what is it?
Also called the ratel, this remarkably loose-skinned mammal — able to twist freely inside its own hide — is the largest land member of the weasel family in Africa. What is it?
Honey badger: Species of mammal. The honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel ( or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
This condition, caused by low blood potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, can bring on fatigue, leg cramps, and a dangerously slow heart rhythm — what is it?
Hypokalemia: Insufficient potassium in the blood. Normal potassium levels in humans are between 3.5 and 5.0 mmol/L (3.5 and 5.0 mEq/L) with levels below 3.5 mmol/L defined as hypokalemia.
Most often extracted from chicory, this plant-stored fructan earned FDA approval as a dietary fiber in 2018 and remains the gold-standard compound for measuring kidney filtration rates — what is it?
Serving as special adviser to the UN Secretary-General from 2002 to 2018, which Columbia University economist co-founded a nonprofit dedicated to ending extreme poverty?
This twin-engine fighter jet program made its home nation the fourth in the world to develop stealth avionics, joining the ranks of the US, China, and Russia — which aircraft?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: South Korean fighter aircraft.
Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine, this spicy Southeast Asian noodle dish is often served in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind — what is it?
Laksa: Spicy noodle dish from Southeast Asia.
This genus of bulb-grown flowering plants, prized for their large blooms, is highly toxic to cats — even though many unrelated plants borrow its common name — which genus?
Lilium: Genus of plants. Lilium ( LIL-ee-əm) is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
This best-known stag beetle species in Western Europe lends its genus its very name, and is currently listed as Near Threatened — what is it?
Lucanus cervus: Species of beetle. L. cervus is listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).
Also known as flying foxes, these 197-plus species of fruit-eating bat likely evolved in Australasia some 31 million years ago — what are they called?

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)
Native to southern Europe and North Africa, this fragrant evergreen shrub has berries that are macerated in alcohol to make Mirto liqueur — which plant?
Myrtus communis: Species of flowering plant.
This Serbian-American engineer designed the modern alternating current electricity supply system—the backbone of today's power grid. Who?
Nikola Tesla: Serbian-American engineer and inventor (1856–1943)
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
Also known as jícama or Mexican turnip, this pea-family vine's edible tuberous root comes in a milky-juice form and a watery-juice form — which species is it?
Pachyrhizus erosus: Species of legume. Pachyrhizus tuberosus and Pachyrhizus ahipa are the other two cultivated species in the genus.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.
This colorless, highly toxic pnictogen hydride is pure when odorless, but technical samples reek of rotting fish — and impurities can make it burst into flame in air — what is it?
Named after a French mathematician and physicist, this materials-science measure captures how much a material bulges sideways when compressed lengthwise — what is it?
Poisson's ratio: Measure of material deformation perpendicular to loading.
Found just below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male-only gland acts like a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation — which organ?
Prostate: Gland of the male reproductive system.
Sold as Seroquel and prescribed for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, this atypical antipsychotic is also widely (and questionably) used as a sleep aid for its tranquillizing effect — which drug?
Quetiapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Quetiapine is believed to work by blocking a number of receptors, including those for serotonin and dopamine.
Native to East Asia but a notorious invasive pest in Europe and North America, this knotweed has won over beekeepers and foragers alike, its young stems tasting of lemony rhubarb. What plant is it?
Native to Eurasia and commonly known simply as the raspberry, this red-fruited bramble is widely cultivated across temperate regions — what species is it?
Nicknamed 'snail fever,' this tropical disease is caused by a parasitic flatworm picked up from freshwater contaminated by infected snails — what is it?
Schistosomiasis: Human disease caused by parasitic worms called schistosomes.

Recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909, this small, clever herding dog breed originated in Scotland's northern isles and was originally called by a different collie name before breeders objected — which breed?
Shetland Sheepdog: Scottish breed of dog. The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?
Shaped roughly like a necktie and made up of the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process, which flat bone protects the heart and lungs at the front of the rib cage?
Sternum: Flat bone in the middle front part of the rib cage.

Caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum, this infection famously hides: a painless ulcer first, then a rash that loves the palms and soles, then years of silent latency before tertiary damage. What is it?
Named from Greek for 'four teeth,' this family includes the pufferfish, blowfish, and toadfish — many of them among the most poisonous vertebrates alive. What is this family called?
Tetraodontidae: Family of pufferfish. Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.

Sold under the brand name Zanaflex, this alpha-2 adrenergic agonist treats muscle spasticity from spinal cord injuries and multiple sclerosis, and racked up over 8 million US prescriptions in 2023 — what is it?
NATO code-named 'Careless,' this three-engined Soviet airliner once carried half of Aeroflot's passengers and could operate from unpaved gravel airstrips in Arctic conditions — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-154: Soviet and Russian medium-range trijet airliner.
A British-American structural biologist who shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for revealing the structure of the ribosome, he later served as President of the Royal Society — who is he?
First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop — which grain?
Wheat: Genus of grass cultivated for grain. Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.

Distinguished by a fatty hump on its shoulders and a large dewlap, this heat-tolerant type of domestic cattle originated in South Asia and holds religious significance in parts of the world — what is it?
Zebu: South Asian domestic cattle. The zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.

The symbol for barium is Ba. Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
